summary: Set limit is a budget card for capping what an agent can spend in a month. A bar shows what has been spent so far and where spending is forecast to land, and the person drags a knob or types a figure to set the cap. A line under the bar warns when the forecast will pass the cap, and a switch decides whether runs pause, ask first or keep going at the limit.
use: When agent runs cost money and a team needs a monthly ceiling
When people should see whether their current pace will go over before it happens
When the team must choose what the agent does at the limit: stop, ask, or continue
When a cap needs to be adjusted quickly by dragging or typing an exact amount
features: The bar shows `spent` as a solid fill and `forecast` as a striped fill up to the cap.
Dragging along the bar snaps the cap to `step`, and the knob glides to new values set any other way.
Clicking the big figure lets the person type a cap; Enter or leaving the field keeps it within `min` and `max`, and Escape restores the old value.
When the forecast passes the cap, the line warns "Forecast passes your cap around Oct 27" and says what runs will do; otherwise it shows the amount left.
The At the limit switch sets `mode` to pause, ask or keep, and `message` can replace the line under the bar.
`format` controls how amounts are written, and the symbols around the number stay in place while typing.
a11y: The knob is a `slider` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and a formatted `aria-valuetext`.
Arrow keys move the cap by `step`, on the slider and in the typed figure.
The warning line is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so going over or back on track is announced.
The At the limit switch is a labelled `group` with `aria-pressed` on each choice.

faq.q: Does this component stop the agent when the cap is reached?
faq.a: No. It shows and sets the cap and the at-the-limit choice. Read them from `onValueChange` and `onModeChange` and enforce them where your runs are billed.

faq.q: How do I show amounts in another currency?
faq.a: Pass `format`, like `n => n + ' €'`. The text around the number stays fixed while someone types a new cap.

faq.q: Can I write my own warning text?
faq.a: Yes. `message` receives whether the forecast is over, the cap, what is left and the mode, and returns what to show under the bar.
